Custom experiment names persist through JSON remounting and export with their notes, release settings, and reference.
Preview is read-only, ignores forged predictions and metadata, and imports selected data without moving the current run or reference. Undo preserves later edits and unrelated work.
The backup reference is an explicit opt-in. Undo restores the previous reference, retains a reference selected later, and keeps experiment numbering monotonic.
Unchanged saved IDs are skipped; conflicting local notes remain intact and the backup becomes a separate record.
The preview shows every incoming record and enforces available capacity without eviction; making room and separate removal/import undo actions preserve all existing notes.
Malformed JSON, unsupported versions, invalid releases, duplicate IDs, and oversized files produce feedback without changing saved data.
Overlapping reads use the latest file; cancellation, mode changes, unmounting, and read failures cannot reopen a stale preview or modify the notebook.
Long names, notes, and filenames remain plain text and fit 1440, 390, 320 px and RTL layouts with accessible selection labels and touch targets.
The release table updates during launch editing and highlights exactly the changed inputs while retaining the saved release.
The dashed reference and cursor sample the same elapsed model time as the current run; keyboard scrubbing announces both centers.
Captured and escaped reference curves end at the exact modeled endpoint, hide their later cursor, and recover when scrubbing backward.
Keeping and clearing a reference recomputes the shared graph scale while preserving playback time, selected debris, and camera view.
Comparison inputs survive an optical view change and a complete JSON remount; reopening rebuilds the same graph after release.
1440, 390, 320 px and RTL layouts keep readable release columns, a dashed reference legend, and valid graph geometry without horizontal overflow.
48 px handles support native mouse/touch placement, keyboard placement and aiming, and Escape rollback without moving the camera or saved reference.
Saving, notes, center outcomes, and paused restore use the release inputs; restoring a run leaves the reference fixed.
Reference geometry and notes survive mode changes and complete unmount/remount from JSON tool data.
Removal is reversible and keeps the independent reference; the eight-entry limit preserves notes, and JSON export includes settings and current model predictions.
Desktop, 390 px, 320 px, and RTL layouts retain usable targets without horizontal overflow.
